UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Represents a user's personal information and preferences within the FitStride application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserProfile entity.

name.description: The user's full name as provided during registration or profile setup.

email.description: The user's email address, used for communication and profile identification.

dateOfBirth.description: The user's date of birth, used for age-related fitness metrics.

unitPreference.description: The user's preferred unit system for measurements (e.g., 'metric', 'imperial').

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the user profile was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the user profile was last updated.

Exercise.title: Exercise
Exercise.description: A catalog of various exercises available in the FitStride application, used for logging workouts and AI suggestions.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Exercise entity.

name.description: The name of the exercise (e.g., 'Running', 'Bench Press', 'Squats').

description.description: A brief description or instructions for the exercise.

category.description: The category the exercise belongs to (e.g., 'Cardio', 'Chest', 'Legs', 'Full Body').

WorkoutSession.title: WorkoutSession
WorkoutSession.description: Represents a single logged workout session by a user, acting as a container for individual exercises performed.

id.description: Unique identifier for the WorkoutSession entity.

sessionDateTime.description: The date and time when the workout session occurred.

durationMinutes.description: The total duration of the workout session in minutes.

notes.description: Any additional notes or comments about the workout session.

estimatedCaloriesBurned.description: The estimated total calories burned during this workout session.

type.description: The general type of workout session (e.g., 'Cardio', 'Strength', 'Mixed', 'Other').

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the workout session was logged.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the workout session was last updated.

LoggedExercise.title: LoggedExercise
LoggedExercise.description: Represents a single exercise performed as part of a WorkoutSession, linking to specific exercise details (CardioDetails or StrengthDetails).

id.description: Unique identifier for the LoggedExercise entity.

orderInSession.description: The sequential order in which this exercise was performed within the workout session.

notes.description: Specific notes for this particular instance of the exercise within the session.

CardioDetails.title: CardioDetails
CardioDetails.description: Stores specific details for a cardio exercise logged within a WorkoutSession.

id.description: Unique identifier for the CardioDetails entity.

distance.description: The distance covered during the cardio exercise.

distanceUnit.description: The unit of measurement for the distance (e.g., 'miles', 'km').

caloriesBurned.description: The estimated calories burned during this specific cardio exercise.

averageSpeed.description: The average speed maintained during the cardio exercise.

heartRateData.description: An array of heart rate readings collected during the cardio exercise.

StrengthDetails.title: StrengthDetails
StrengthDetails.description: Stores general details for a strength training exercise logged within a WorkoutSession, acting as a container for individual sets.

id.description: Unique identifier for the StrengthDetails entity.

totalSets.description: The total number of sets performed for this strength exercise.

totalReps.description: The total number of repetitions performed across all sets for this strength exercise.

oneRepMaxEstimate.description: An estimated one-repetition maximum for this exercise instance, based on logged sets and reps.

SetDetails.title: SetDetails
SetDetails.description: Records the specifics of a single set performed during a strength training exercise.

id.description: Unique identifier for the SetDetails entity.

setNumber.description: The sequential number of the set within the strength exercise.

reps.description: The number of repetitions performed in this set.

weight.description: The weight lifted for this set.

weightUnit.description: The unit of measurement for the weight (e.g., 'lbs', 'kg').

FitnessGoal.title: FitnessGoal
FitnessGoal.description: Defines a fitness goal set by a user, allowing for tracking and progress visualization.

id.description: Unique identifier for the FitnessGoal entity.

name.description: A short, descriptive name for the fitness goal.

description.description: A more detailed description of the goal.

targetValue.description: The numerical target value for the goal (e.g., 10 for '10 miles', 3 for '3 workouts/week').

targetUnit.description: The unit corresponding to the target value (e.g., 'miles', 'times/week', 'kg', 'lbs', 'calories').

startDate.description: The date when the fitness goal was started.

endDate.description: The date when the fitness goal is expected to be completed or reviewed.

status.description: The current status of the goal (e.g., 'Active', 'Completed', 'Achieved', 'Failed', 'Paused').

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the fitness goal was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the fitness goal was last updated.

firestore.reasoning:
The recommended Firestore structure for FitStride prioritizes security, scalability, and debuggability by strictly adhering to the core design principles. The structure uses a hierarchical, user-centric model for all personal data and a flat, global collection for shared, read-only data. 

**Authorization Independence (CRITICAL):** This design achieves Authorization Independence by explicitly denormalizing the `userId` into *every* document that belongs to a specific user. For example, `WorkoutSession`, `LoggedExercise`, `CardioDetails`, `StrengthDetails`, `SetDetails`, and `FitnessGoal` documents will all contain a `userId` field matching the `id` of the owning `UserProfile`. This allows Firestore Security Rules to directly check `request.auth.uid == resource.data.userId` and `request.auth.uid == userId` (from the path wildcard) on any document operation without needing to perform `get()` calls to parent documents to verify ownership. This avoids complex rule logic, prevents breaking atomic write operations (like transactions or batched writes), and significantly improves rule performance and debuggability.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters):** This structure supports Query-Aware Permissions (QAPs) through robust structural segregation:
1.  **Private User Data:** All user-specific data is stored under `/users/{userId}/...`. Security rules will enforce that `request.auth.uid` must match the `{userId}` wildcard in the path for any read or write operation within these subcollections. This guarantees that `list` operations (queries) for a user's `workoutSessions`, `fitnessGoals`, or nested data will *only* return data owned by the authenticated user, without needing client-side filtering or server-side rule-based filtering that incurs performance penalties and security risks. The structure inherently prevents unauthorized users from even attempting to query another user's private data.
2.  **Public Catalog Data:** The `/exercises/{exerciseId}` collection is a global, read-only catalog. Rules will permit `read` access to all authenticated users. This clear segregation ensures that querying `/exercises` will yield a complete list of available exercises for all users, again without requiring filtering by rules.

**General Principles:**
*   **Structural Segregation:** Data with different security postures (private user data vs. public catalog) is placed in distinct top-level collections, simplifying security rules immensely.
*   **Access Modeling:** Path-based ownership (`/users/{userId}/...`) is consistently used for all user-owned data, creating a clear and intuitive hierarchy. This ensures that a user's `WorkoutSession` is nested under their `UserProfile`, and `LoggedExercise` under `WorkoutSession`, and so on, making ownership self-evident in the path.
*   **Data Clarity:** Wildcards are descriptive (e.g., `{userId}`, `{workoutSessionId}`), and the explicit `userId` field provides clear ownership metadata within each document.
